narration.text: Welcome to freeway, flex and express lane rules. Flex lanes can reverse direction by time of day, so the overhead signal controls whether you may enter. On the freeway keep at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead, and lengthen that gap when weather or visibility worsens. This session connects signal obedience, spacing, lane courtesy and ramp discipline into one clear routine you can use every trip.

Flex lanes may reverse direction by time of day, which is why you must check the overhead signal before entering. A green arrow means you may use the lane right now, while a red cross means the lane is closed to you. Never guess from habit or from other drivers, because the allowed direction can change. Make the signal check part of every flex lane entry, just like checking a traffic light before proceeding through an intersection.

On the freeway keep at least two seconds of following distance, and make the gap larger when rain, fog, heavy traffic or poor visibility reduce control. A larger gap gives time to see slowing ahead and brake smoothly without swerving. If you drive in the left lane and a faster vehicle approaches from behind, move safely right so it can pass. Lingering on the left can draw a citation for impeding, so treat moving right as both courtesy and legal duty.

Express lanes on the interstate are free for vehicles with two or more occupants, plus motorcycles, buses and registered clean fuel decal vehicles. Qualifying matters, but location matters too. Crossing a double white line to enter or leave is prohibited. Enter or exit only at dotted line access points. Waiting for the dotted opening keeps merges predictable and prevents sudden crossings in front of through traffic in the express lane.

lines.text: Occupancy alone does not authorize crossing.
Dotted opening still required every time.

narration.text: Here is a trap that confuses many learners. Flex direction follows the overhead signal, while express entry follows occupancy plus dotted access points. Having two occupants qualifies you for toll free use, but it never allows crossing a double white line. You still must wait for a dotted access point. Remember the pair together: qualify by occupants, then move only where dotted lines permit entry or exit.

Pause and retrieve the express lane entry rule from memory. Ask yourself where along the express lane a driver may legally move in or out. The answer is only at dotted access points, because crossing a double white line is prohibited. If you recalled dotted openings rather than any convenient gap, you have the rule. Keep that image of solid double lines as a wall and dotted lines as a door.

To close, lock in ramp and prohibition rules. Ramp meters show alternating red and green and generally release one vehicle per green, obeyed only when the meter on sign is lit. Runaway ramps are for emergency stops only, with no stopping or parking on them. U turns on the freeway are prohibited, as is driving or stopping for passengers outside the solid white line. The single point off ramp turnaround is allowed only facing a green arrow, and you must finish once started.

why_how.text: Overhead signals control flex lanes because direction reverses by time of day, so checking prevents head on conflict.
Two second gaps plus moving right for faster traffic keep flow smooth and avoid impeding citations.
Express toll free use depends on occupants and vehicle type, while dotted access points keep merges orderly.
Ramp meters pace entry one vehicle per green when lit, which reduces sudden freeway slowdowns.
Bans on freeway turnarounds and emergency lane misuse plus emergency only runaway ramps preserve escape paths.

narration.text: Welcome to intersections, markings, signals and right of way. At every intersection slow down and scan for controls, cross traffic, walkers, riders and blocked views, and never assume others will yield. Stop fully behind signs, signals, walks or stop lines, and when queued leave room to see the rear tires ahead. This session builds a calm approach habit, clear stop position, marking meaning, signal meaning and yielding judgment.

Approach every intersection by slowing and searching for signals, signs, oncoming and cross traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists and sight blocks. Do not rely on others to obey controls. Come to a complete stop behind any stop sign, signal, sidewalk or stop line. When queued behind another vehicle, keep enough space to see its rear tires. At a sign or signal stop behind the stop line or crosswalk and grant passage to anyone in or entering any crosswalk, marked or not.

Center markings guide passing and turning. Broken yellow center lines permit passing when safe, while solid lines and double center lines restrict or bar passing as marked. Enter a shared center left turn lane no more than five hundred feet before the turn, after mirrors, signal and blind spot check. For speed, defaults absent signs or hazards are twenty near schools during recess or arrival and dismissal, twenty five in business and residential areas, and fifty five on major highways as posted. Reduce speed at intersections, rail crossings, curves, hill crests, narrow or winding roads, work zones and whenever sight or control is reduced.

Signals and yielding connect directly to your approach habit. Steady yellow means the signal is about to turn red, while flashing yellow means slow, proceed with care and be ready to stop. A flashing yellow arrow permits the turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and walkers, who hold the green. Right on red is allowed after a full stop unless posted otherwise, but red arrows require waiting for a go indication. Grant the way to the vehicle already inside, to oncoming traffic on a left turn, to the driver on the right at a tied four way stop, and to road traffic when leaving a drive. At rail tracks cross promptly without stopping on them, waiting until arms rise and lights end when gates operate.

Now test the crosswalk rule in your own words. At a sign controlled crossing, who must you let pass and where do you stop. The answer is stop behind the line and allow anyone in or entering any crosswalk to pass, marked or not. Stopping behind keeps the walkway clear and preserves sight lines. If you included both unmarked crossings and entering walkers, your understanding is solid and ready for the road.

To finish, fix signs and roundabouts in memory. Warning signs are generally diamond shaped yellow with black symbols, while guide signs are square or rectangular green, brown or blue. Work zone signs are diamond or rectangular orange with black legends, and speeding fines in work zones are doubled. For roundabouts slow on approach, yield to traffic inside and to walkers, enter when clear, then exit at the wanted street. Carry these images forward: yellow diamonds warn, orange zones demand extra care, and roundabouts reward patience.

why_how.text: Scanning plus never assuming priority prevents crashes because others may fail to yield.
Stopping behind lines and yielding in all crosswalks keeps walkers visible and paths clear.
Broken versus solid markings and short center lane entry separate passing from turning safely.
Default limits plus hazard slowing match speed to schools, neighborhoods, highways and reduced sight.
Yellow caution, yield first arrows and red arrow waiting prevent rushed turns against priority traffic.

narration.text: Welcome to the full rules spine, linking lanes, intersections, signals, signs and yielding. Flex use follows the overhead signal, with green arrow open and red cross closed. Intersection success starts with slowing and scanning, stopping behind the line, looking left right left, crossing without lane change, then merging right. This session weaves those habits together so each rule supports the next, from freeway discipline through novel interchanges to signal obedience and courteous yielding.

Freeway discipline starts with keeping the following gap and avoiding turnarounds, emergency lane driving and ramp reversal. A left lane vehicle approached from behind must move right to avoid impeding. Express use needs qualifying occupancy, with double white crossing barred except at dotted access points. Single occupant use needs a paid pass account, while a clean fuel decal is a separate windshield authorization. Think gap kept, courtesy given, qualification checked and dotted entry used.

Entering and leaving need smooth timing. Use the acceleration lane to match speed, exit early and steady, and pass a metered ramp one vehicle per green. Runaway ramps are emergency only with no stopping, while the single point off ramp turnaround is allowed on green arrow and must be finished once started, never stopping mid crossing. Continuous flow, diverging diamond and thru turn layouts each redirect left turns, so follow staged signals and lane guides rather than improvising a direct left.

Intersection and marking discipline work as a pair. Approach slow and scan, stop behind the line, look left right left, cross without lane change, then merge right. Yellow divides opposing flow while white divides same direction flow. Stop behind the line and yield in crosswalks, with shared center lane entry limited before the turn. The basic law is reasonable and prudent speed, with posted defaults by area, slowing for hazards, and no impeding that can be cited. Markings show position, speed shows judgment.

Signal meanings reward careful reading. Green means go if clear, green arrow allows only the arrow direction after yielding, yellow warns red is near, and flashing yellow means caution. Red means stop and wait, with right on red after stop unless barred, flashing red as stop then go, and red arrows requiring a wait. An officer overrides any signal, and a dead signal needs stop first. Guide signs inform, railroad crossings need caution and stop discipline, regulatory signs command, warning diamonds alert, and work zone orange brings doubled speeding fines plus flagger obedience.

This trap separates green from red thinking. Green and yellow allow movement with clearance and caution, while red requires stopping and waiting, with only narrow turn after stop rules. The confusion is treating green as automatic go and red as negotiable. Correct thinking is green go if clear, green arrow only arrow direction after yielding, flashing yellow caution, red stop and wait, flashing red stop then go, and officer instructions beating every light. Hold both sides in mind before choosing to move.

Retrieve the green and yellow family now. What care does a green light, a green arrow and a yellow light each require. Answer in your mind: go if clear on green, arrow direction only after yielding, caution on yellow with red near, and extra caution on flashing yellow. If your answer tied clearance to green, direction limits to arrows and preparation to stop to yellow, you have separated the indications correctly.

We close with yielding judgment. Never assume priority. Yield to prior arrival, oncoming traffic on a left turn, the right side tie, driveway entrants, ramp yields and anyone still inside the intersection. That rule completes the approach routine of slowing, stopping behind, triple looking and holding lane. Carry one sentence forward: scan first, respect signals and markings, choose reasonable speed, and yield whenever another user holds priority.

Green clearance, red waiting, officer priority and sign classes translate indications into action.
